channel.title: Study Smarter
channel.description: Study methods backed by research, explained simply.

item.title: How Many Hours a Week Should You Study in College?
item.description: What the federal credit hour definition implies about weekly study time, with the math for 12 and 15 credits and a plan for spreading the hours out.

item.title: Interleaved Practice: Why Mixing Problem Types Works
item.description: What classroom trials found when math practice mixed different problem types instead of grouping them, and how to build interleaving into homework.

item.title: Active Recall vs Rereading: What the Research Found
item.description: What the 2006 Roediger and Karpicke testing effect study found when comparing retrieval practice to repeated rereading for long-term retention.

item.title: Spaced Repetition: How It Works and How to Use It
item.description: What the 2008 Cepeda et al spacing effect study found about the ideal gap between study sessions relative to how long you need to remember something.

item.title: The Cornell Note-Taking Method Explained
item.description: A step-by-step look at the five-part Cornell note-taking system from Cornell University's Learning Strategies Center, and how each step is used.

item.title: Two Study Habits Beyond Flashcards and Spaced Review
item.description: An explanation of interleaving worked examples with practice problems and asking deep questions, two habits from a federal education practice guide.
